title: New schedule opens an empty Untitled schedule editor; first Save keeps it open
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in, on the build under test, as an Owner/Admin or as a user with "Settings Service" enabled.
  2. In the left sidebar under Settings, open the "Maintenance" entry beneath "Inspection Templates" (if the build shows "Maintenance schedules" instead, use that entry and record the label). Schedules are shared by the whole organization, whichever location is chosen in the header.
custom_steps:
1. In Settings > Maintenance click New schedule.
  2. Read the editor that opens: its title, and whether any modal or template chooser appears.
  3. Without saving, leave the editor (click another Settings entry), come back to the schedule list and look for a draft.
  4. Click New schedule again, add one service (Add service, name "PM-A", calendar Every 3 months, save the service) and click Save on the schedule.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • New schedule opens straight into an empty editor titled "Untitled schedule"; no modal and no template to choose.
  • Nothing was left behind: the list shows no draft for the editor you left without saving.
  • After the first Save the editor stays open on the saved schedule and a success message (toast) appears; the schedule is now in the list.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-3780, story SV-10558 (S1, Create a maintenance schedule), Chunk 1 MR (Confluence 886931488) as edited 5 October 2026, S1 (New schedule; S1-R3, S1-R4); Plan 1 — Track, act, clear — Technical Implementation Plan, section 3.1 Settled decisions, D21; read 6 Oct 2026. Source-verified 6 October 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S1-R3: “New schedule opens an empty editor titled Untitled schedule. There is no modal and no template”
  • S1-R4: “A schedule exists from its first Save. Leaving the editor before that leaves nothing behind”
  • Plan 1 §3.1 D21: “After the first Save of a new schedule the editor stays open, does `router.replace` to the schedule's `/:id` route and shows a success toast”
